new_page.title: Richmond Condos for Sale | Prices by Neighbourhood
new_page.description: Search Richmond condos for sale. See what Brighouse, West Cambie and Steveston condos sold for, with strata fees by building and the benchmark price.

faq.q: How much is a condo in Richmond?
faq.a: The median Richmond condo sold for about $620,000 in Brighouse, $630,500 in West Cambie and $675,000 in Steveston South over the year to October 22, 2026. The apartment benchmark for the city was $635,600 in September 2026.

faq.q: Where do most Richmond condos sell?
faq.a: Brighouse, with 479 of 1,095 sales, then West Cambie with 236 and Brighouse South with 121.

faq.q: What are strata fees for a Richmond condo?
faq.a: Median monthly fees by neighbourhood ran from $420 in Hamilton to $582 in Ironwood, with $514 in Brighouse. The building decides, so check the fee in the listing.

faq.q: Which Richmond condo neighbourhoods are newest?
faq.a: Hamilton (median built 2026), Bridgeport (2018) and West Cambie (2017).
The apartment benchmark price moved -9.1% over one year and -14.0% over three years, to $635,600 in September 2026.

faq.q: Where do I find the rules for buying a strata?
faq.a: On the BC condo buying rules page. It covers the strata documents you are entitled to and what to read before you remove subjects.

blocks.text: This search lists condos for sale in Richmond: apartment-style homes in strata buildings, from the towers around Richmond Centre to the low-rises in Steveston. Houses and townhomes are separate searches.

1,095 Richmond condos closed in the year to October 22, 2026, in 14 neighbourhoods. Brighouse alone had 479 of them, 44% of the city, at a median of $620,000. The sold records report Richmond by neighbourhood, so I give neighbourhood medians instead of one city number.

blocks.text: Age matters as much as location. West Cambie’s condos were built around 2017 and sold at a median of $630,500, which is $834 a square foot. Brighouse South’s were built around 1991 and sold at $535,000, or $552 a square foot. Hamilton’s median year built is 2026, which means a lot of those sales were in new buildings.

Strata fees run from $420 a month in Hamilton to $574 in Steveston South and $582 in Ironwood. Brighouse sits at $514. Fees tell you what the building covers, so compare them alongside price, not after.

blocks.text: A building’s price here comes from its own closed sales, so a tower with 20 sales says more than one with 5. Buildings with fewer than 5 sales are left out, because one or two sales is not a price.

Richmond is protected by 49 kilometres of dikes, and Richmond Fire-Rescue says pockets of liquefaction are possible in a significant earthquake. Ask the strata about building insurance, the depreciation report and any past water damage before you offer. The BC condo buying rules page covers the strata documents.

items.t: Ask for the strata minutes and the depreciation report, and read the last two years of minutes for special levies.
Check what the monthly fee includes. Ironwood ($582) and Steveston South ($574) sit above Brighouse ($514).
Check whether the building allows rentals and pets before you offer.
For a new building in Hamilton, ask for the occupancy date and the status of the common areas.
